# TSMP Core 0.3.0-beta.1

Beta preview of TransSync send scheduling, Timeline synchronization fixes, and FFmpeg publishing stability improvements. This release adds functionality as well as bug fixes; the stable release remains 0.2.0.

## Added: TransSync send scheduling

- Implement `Priority`, `SendOnChange`, and `MinSendInterval` in both native Unity and Udon.
- Consider higher-priority fields first and rotate equally prioritized fields after successful output.
- Detect serialized-content changes, including edits to existing arrays. Measure minimum intervals from successful frame output.
- Refresh unchanged values every second by default. Set the Encoder's `transSyncRefreshInterval` to zero to disable refresh.
- Preserve send state when output fails or a field does not fit. Reserve queued RPC payload before automatic variables, and defer oversized fields without truncation.
- Preserve the output texture and frame index when no variable or RPC is eligible.

## Fixed: Timeline synchronization

- Apply the first received playback position and prepare paused graphs correctly.
- Avoid repeated graph reconstruction for stopped packets.
- Correct Continuous receive drift, including loop boundaries, and clear stale corrections when reception or the Director changes.
- Reject malformed packets before applying playback state.
- Improve Play/Resume after Stop and add `Seek(float)` with playback-state preservation.

## Fixed: FFmpeg publishing

- Reject source/output resolution mismatches before starting FFmpeg instead of silently corrupting raw frames. TSMP pixels are never implicitly resized.
- Validate source changes and completed RGBA32 readbacks before row flipping or submission.
- Isolate processes, buffers, GPU callbacks and diagnostics by publishing session.
- Replace `Thread.Interrupt()` with cooperative shutdown and process termination for blocked pipes. Handle failed startup, unexpected process exit, disable and restart without mixing sessions.

## Updating and compatibility

- VCC: enable prerelease versions for TSMP Core in the repository at https://vpm.kiba.red/ and select 0.3.0-beta.1. Use TSMP Codec Luma4 0.0.3 or newer.
- Ordinary Unity: install Core and Luma4 through UPM; VRCSDK is optional. FFmpeg publishing remains native desktop functionality, not an Udon process running inside VRChat.
- Allow Unity to refresh bindings and recompile UdonSharp programs after updating.
- `SendOnChange` defaults to true and now affects actual traffic. Set `SendOnChange = false, MinSendInterval = 0` to retain unconditional per-encode sending. Automatic refresh is best effort, not acknowledged delivery; strict priority can starve lower-priority fields under overload.
- FFmpeg dimensions and frame rate are fixed at session startup. Stop and restart after changing them. YUV420p requires even dimensions.
- Packet layouts and codec IDs are unchanged. Receiver frame application and interpolation policies outside Timeline are unchanged.
- In Udon, control Timeline playback through the sync component. Direct external Director controls and automatic completion remain limited by the exposed Udon APIs.

## Validation

Validated with Unity 2022.3.22f1, Luma4 0.0.3, Worlds SDK 3.10.4-beta.2 with bundled UdonSharp, and Direct3D11 on an RTX 4090:

- Native TransSync scheduling and Timeline regression suites.
- Real Udon VM scheduling checks and full UdonSharp client compilation.
- Actual Luma4 GPU encode/decode loopback in the Editor and Windows x64 Mono Player, including Transform, animated Humanoid/Timeline, Unicode fields and RPCs.
- Thirteen FFmpeg regression cases in native and SDK-present Editors and the Windows Mono Player, including actual FFmpeg output, Texture2D/RenderTexture inputs, vertical flip, repeated restart and blocked-stdin shutdown.
- English, Korean and Japanese documentation builds.

One existing Luma4 shader warning remains in the Core loopback build. IL2CPP/stripping, Quest, a remote RTMP service, SDK world build and an uploaded VRChat client were not validated for this release. Package publishing success is separate from runtime validation. Reproduction instructions and evidence are under `Validation~/`.
